_comment: Single source of truth for the location inner pages, the way
shared/segments.json is for the paid segment pages. Two registries, not
one, because they answer different questions: segments.json fixes six
HubSpot routing strings that never change, this file lists the places the
client has picked.
READ locations/PLAN.md FIRST, dated 2 Sep 2026. It is the rules layer for
this family and it supersedes locations/STRATEGY.md, REFERENCE.md and
BRIEF.md of 21 Aug 2026, all three of which are now in
locations/_archive/. Where a decision below predates PLAN.md and PLAN.md
disagrees, PLAN.md wins and the entry says so.
SCOPE SET 21 Aug 2026 AND UNCHANGED: one template, three pages. Adelaide,
Perth and Melbourne. What changed on 2 Sep 2026 is where the template
comes from. Melbourne and Adelaide are live HubSpot pages running the same
template as Brisbane, so two of the three are replacements of ranking URLs
rather than new pages, and the shared template cannot be what makes
Brisbane rank. See openDecisions.templateNotFormula and
openDecisions.replacementInventory.
URL pattern is the client's existing one, /location/<slug>, so these pages
are siblings of a page that already ranks rather than new competitors for
the homepage. The slug is the URL segment and the folder name, and the two
never differ.
'readiness' is what the page can honestly carry today, not a build status.
It is separate from status on purpose: a page can be unblocked to build and
still be unable to fill a slot. Perth is the case that forced the split.
DECISIONS THAT SPAN BOTH PAGE FAMILIES LIVE IN segments.json, not here.
The CSS layer split of 21 Aug 2026 is recorded there under
openDecisions.cssLayerSplit. This file only carries decisions that affect
the location pages alone.

locations.label: Melbourne
locations.readiness: PLANNED AGAIN 2 Sep 2026, and now a replacement rather than a new page. /location/melbourne is live and ranking, so openDecisions.replacementInventory applies before any copy is written. Phase 2 of PLAN.md writes the copy deck, phase 3 builds the page. The two audited proof records and the capture contract carry forward from the archived build; its composition does not.
locations.office: yes, named in the client supplied office list
locations.proof: Two of three filled and audited clean. Geoff, Melbourne office, May 2025, $3,908,748 against a $4,172,548 appraisal, commercial deck p.7, and absent from the investor deck. Wendy, 2024, $1,175,000 on a 5.0 percent initial yield, $1,400,000 in 2026, $225,000 equity created, investor deck p37, figures verified against that deck directly. THE THIRD SLOT IS BLOCKED ON THE CLIENT: both Melbourne home buyer candidates are re-narrated in the investor deck as investments, one with identical figures. See openDecisions.melbourneThirdProofContested.
locations.note: The template for the family, and the honest test of it. Its bracketed slots and their owners are numbered in locations/PLAN.md section 8.
locations.paper: Artboard 'MELBOURNE · 1440' in the Paper file 'Location Pages - Adelaide, Perth, Melbourne'. Client-approved, and edited once since approval: the 8 Sep 2026 language pass changed seventeen strings, all grammar, punctuation or bracket convention, no claim, figure, name or layout. See openDecisions.melbourneLanguagePass. There is no Melbourne COPY.md yet, so when phase 2 writes one it must be written from the corrected artboard.
locations.archived: locations/_archive/melbourne-2026-08-21/, archived 2 Sep 2026. Built 21 Aug 2026 and passing every hard rule, but composed from the live Brisbane page on the assumption that Brisbane structure is why Brisbane ranks. PLAN.md section 0 retired that assumption. See openDecisions.templateNotFormula, and the README in that folder for the three things that carry forward.

locations.label: Adelaide
locations.readiness: DESIGNED IN PAPER 8 Sep 2026, awaiting client review. The artboard 'ADELAIDE· 1440' carries the full Adelaide copy, imagery and three proof cards; locations/adelaide/COPY.md is the record of it and ends with the preserved-from-live table the replacementInventory rule asks for. The HTML page is not built; PLAN.md builds Melbourne first. Client supply items on the design: the segment framing for all three proof records (openDecisions.adelaideProofFramingContested), a tracked SA number, office hours, sourced market figures, four Adelaide testimonials, inner south suburbs and Hills towns.
locations.office: yes, 224 Hutt Street, Adelaide SA 5000, on the live page and in the site footer. No local phone number is published; the live page carries 1300 only
locations.team: Jonathon Moore, Senior Buyers' Advocate, is the only SA based person on the client's team page, read 8 Sep 2026. He is card 1 on the design; the six national cards carry over from the client-approved Melbourne artboard, flagged in COPY.md for the client to keep or drop
locations.proof: Three records on the design, figures only: Karl (Adelaide, 2008, $400,000, $1,050,000 in 2026), Peter (Adelaide, 2009, $365,000, $1,050,000), Li (regional SA, 2025, $617,000, $750,000). All five SA records in the client's material appear in BOTH Legacy decks with identical figures and opposite framings, so the segment pill on each card is bracketed. See paper/proof-register.md, 'Adelaide location page'.
locations.paper: Artboard 'ADELAIDE· 1440' in the Paper file 'Location Pages - Adelaide, Perth, Melbourne', updated 8 Sep 2026

locations.label: Perth
locations.readiness: STILL BLOCKED 8 Sep 2026, AND NOW CHECKED EXHAUSTIVELY. locations/perth/BLOCKED.md lists what was checked (all five decks page by page, the team page, the office list, the URL) and the three things that unblock it: a named agent who has bought in Perth, one Perth purchase with month, year and price, and which office runs Perth briefs. The Paper artboard 'PERTH· 1440' was updated to the PLAN.md section 5 variant the same day so the client can see the honest page and its gaps; locations/perth/COPY.md records it. No HTML is built.
locations.office: NO. The office list supplied by the client and recorded independently in paper/commercial-copy.md and paper/investor-copy.md is Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide. Perth is not in it, and the site footer confirms it.
locations.proof: None, and none available. Zero Perth or WA records across all five client decks, checked page by page 8 Sep 2026 and recorded in paper/decks/README.md.
locations.note: See openDecisions.perthHasATeamSection first: the page KEEPS its team section, because Propertybuyer has agents for each location. Do not remove it. Then openDecisions.perthHasNoLocalPresence and openDecisions.perthVariantInPaper, both partly superseded by it. Two slots rather than three still cannot be filled honestly, the office block and the purchase proof, and PLAN.md section 5 removes those rather than emptying them. Perth is also the only new URL of the three, so it has no rankings to protect.
locations.team: The section is on the artboard and still carries the Adelaide names it was copied from. It needs the Perth agents, their titles, the areas they cover and their photographs. That is item 1 in locations/perth/BLOCKED.md and it is the change that moves this page most.
locations.paper: Artboard 'PERTH· 1440' in the Paper file 'Location Pages - Adelaide, Perth, Melbourne', updated to the variant 8 Sep 2026

ownLayout.decision: The location pages take their own layout. They are not derived from the buyer page the way a segment page is. What carries over is the design language and the context, not the page structure: the same Figma tokens, the same two faces, the same base components, the same voice, banned language, claim tiers and proof discipline, and the same DESIGN.md and HANDOVER.md.
ownLayout.status: RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026, from the design lead
ownLayout.consequence: assets/css/locations.css is expected to become a substantial layer rather than a thin one. Nothing is lifted out of landing.css on the assumption it will be reused: its 1330 lines are almost entirely the composition of the buyer page, and that composition does not apply here. The site header and footer are the only likely exception, and are the one open promotion, noted at the top of locations.css.
ownLayout.contrast: The segment pages are built by copying New Builds/buyer/index.html and changing only the copy and the data-segment attribute. That instruction is the one thing from the segment build that does not carry over to this family.

hubspotDelivery.decision: These pages ship in HubSpot, not on Vercel. What this repository produces is the reference implementation that gets handed to the client developer to port: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no framework and no React. The Vercel deploy is a preview for review and handoff, not the host.
hubspotDelivery.status: RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026, from the design lead
hubspotDelivery.consequence: The constraint is already met and must stay met. This repository has no build step, no framework and no CDN dependency, and that is now a handoff requirement rather than a preference. Nothing here may grow a compile step, a component framework or a runtime dependency, because the receiving developer works in HubSpot templates.
hubspotDelivery.watch: Two things travel badly into HubSpot and are worth designing around rather than discovering late. The asset paths are ../../ relative and become HubSpot file manager URLs, so keep every reference in one place rather than scattered inline. The two faces are self hosted from assets/fonts and need uploading to the HubSpot file manager with the same cache headers, or the largest contentful paint regresses on the H1.

seoCannibalisation.problem: DESIGN.md records that the propertybuyer.com.au homepage H1 is untouchable because it holds position one for the core commercial terms, and that this constrains what a landing page H1 may compete with.
seoCannibalisation.status: MOSTLY ANSWERED 21 Aug 2026 BY THE REFERENCE PAGE
seoCannibalisation.answer: These pages slot into an existing pattern, /location/<slug>, alongside a Brisbane page that already ranks and carries a self referencing canonical. They are siblings of a working page rather than new competitors for the homepage, so the constraint that worried me is much narrower than it looked. A city page targeting "buyers agent <city>" is not competing with the homepage for the generic term.
seoCannibalisation.remaining: ANSWERED 2 Sep 2026: they exist. /location/melbourne and /location/adelaide are live HubSpot pages running the Brisbane template, and /location/perth does not exist, with an empty nav link where it would be. So two of the three are replacements of ranking URLs and one is new, which is a materially different job to publishing three new pages. See openDecisions.replacementInventory for the rule that follows, and openDecisions.templateNotFormula for what the shared template does and does not tell us.

locationPageSegmentField.problem: On a segment page the segment is fixed by the page and the visitor types the location. A location page inverts that.
locationPageSegmentField.recommendation: Prefill location from the page and leave it editable. Do not lock it. Somebody on the Melbourne page may be buying in Geelong, and a locked field turns that into a mislabelled lead, which is worse than an unasked question. Prefilled costs nothing and keeps the HubSpot payload identical to the paid pages.
locationPageSegmentField.consequence: The form becomes three steps rather than four: segment, budget band, contact. That removes one field from a form whose own research names budget, phone and timeframe as the fields that suppress completion, so it is a conversion gain rather than only a tidy up.

handWrittenOrGenerated.problem: Whether the location pages need a generator, given the repository deliberately has no build step and that is now a handoff requirement.
handWrittenOrGenerated.answer: No generator. One template, three pages, confirmed by the design lead. Three hand written pages is below the threshold where a generator earns its cost, and HubSpot repeats a template across rows itself, so the multiplication belongs at the destination rather than here. What is handed over is the reference pages, locations.css and the copy decks.

perthHasNoLocalPresence.problem: Perth is one of the three chosen locations, and the client has no Perth office and no Perth proof records. The office list they supplied is Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide, recorded independently in two copy decks. The proof register holds zero Perth records across 75 plus, and commercial-copy.md states outright that no record is in Perth, Adelaide or Canberra.
perthHasNoLocalPresence.consequence: Three sections of the Brisbane template assume a local presence: "Our purchases in <City>", "Your local <City> buyers' agents" with 14 named agents, and "Contact our nearest office". On a Perth page all three are empty. Filling them claims a local office and local purchases that do not exist, which is not a copy problem but a truthfulness one, and it is the exact thing DESIGN.md rule one forbids.
options: Ask the client whether a Perth office or Perth purchases exist and were simply never supplied. Cheapest answer if it is yes.

Build Perth on a variant with those three sections removed rather than emptied, and say so on the page: served from the nearest office, inspected in person. That is the claim the copy decks already make and it is true.
Drop Perth and build Adelaide and Melbourne. Two honest pages beat three where one cannot support its own structure.
perthHasNoLocalPresence.doNot: Do not fill the three slots with records from other cities, and do not name agents who are not in Perth. Do not soften this because the brief asks for three pages.
perthHasNoLocalPresence.partlySuperseded: 8 Sep 2026, by openDecisions.perthHasATeamSection. The client lead states Propertybuyer has agents for each location, Perth included, so the 'no local team' half of this entry is wrong and the Perth page keeps its team section. What still holds is the office (there is none in Perth) and the purchase proof (zero Perth records across all five decks). The doNot above also still holds in the form that matters: name the Perth agents, not agents from other states.

referencePageIsNotACopyModel.decision: The live Brisbane page is the structural and SEO reference for this family. It is not the design or copy model. Its anatomy, its 23 sections, its SEO gaps and its three conflicts with DESIGN.md are recorded in locations/_archive/REFERENCE.md.
referencePageIsNotACopyModel.status: RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026 as to structure, OPEN as to voice
referencePageIsNotACopyModel.open: The page that performs is written in the voice the current design system was created to replace. Its meta description opens with "Discover the expertise of", and discover is on the banned CTA list. Its H1 second line is typed in capitals, which is what the Proyale capitals decision explicitly ruled out. Its authority claim is unquantified. Either this family carries an explicit voice exception, or the new pages apply the new voice and diverge from the page used as evidence. Both are defensible, guessing is not, and the choice is visible to the client.
referencePageIsNotACopyModel.supersededInPart: 2 Sep 2026, by openDecisions.templateNotFormula. The anatomy is retired as a brief because Melbourne and Adelaide share it. What holds is the second half of this entry, the voice conflict, and PLAN.md resolves it: the new pages apply the new voice, and the ranking layer inventory in PLAN.md section 2 is what protects the signals the old voice was carrying.

finalUrlExpansionCollision.problem: paper/context-segments.md records that Performance Max Final URL Expansion is on by default and lets Google replace the chosen landing page with any indexable page on the domain, so a page can be built, paid for and then quietly bypassed. It must be off for the lead generation campaigns. Three new indexable, high intent, conversion tuned city pages enlarge the surface for exactly that substitution.
finalUrlExpansionCollision.status: OPEN, CONFIRM BEFORE THESE PAGES ARE INDEXED
finalUrlExpansionCollision.consequence: If the setting is on when these pages go live, paid budget starts landing on pages that carry no campaign labelling, and the segment attribution the paid pages were built to produce is muddied at the source. The failure is silent: the pages still convert, the labels are just wrong.
finalUrlExpansionCollision.note: The converse is also a decision rather than a default. If a location page later out converts a segment page and somebody wants to point paid traffic at it, that should be its own Final URL with its own labelling, not the result of leaving a default on.

locationBudgetBands.problem: The capture form needs budget bands and a location page serves every segment at once, so no one band set is right for all of them.
locationBudgetBands.assumed: The residential set from the buyer page: under-650k, 650k-1m, 1m-1.5m, 1.5m-2m, 2m-plus. Residential intent dominates the organic query these pages target, and reusing the existing option values keeps the HubSpot payload identical to the paid pages.
locationBudgetBands.consequence: A commercial buyer lands in 2m-plus, which is coarse but not wrong. Changing option values after launch breaks HubSpot routing the same way the segment strings do, so confirm before the page takes traffic.

noPocOnLocationPages.decision: The location pages carry no data-poc, no data-experts-count and no demo availability toggle. The paid pages must delete those before launch; a family born after that lesson does not inherit the debt.
noPocOnLocationPages.consequence: npm run check passes a location page outright, with no known deliberate failure to explain away.

melbourneThirdProofContested.problem: The Melbourne page needs a home buyer record for its third Tier 1 slot. The proof register named two Melbourne candidates from the home buyer deck and recorded them as an extraction job needing nothing from the client. Checked against Legacy All Investor.pdf on 21 Aug 2026, both are also in that deck, narrated as investments.
melbourneThirdProofContested.evidence: Stephen and Melanie, CONFIRMED: the investor deck holds Melbourne VIC, 2013, $2,500,000, 2026 value $4,200,000, equity created $1,700,000, let at $2,000 pw, 3.6 percent initial yield, on a prestige backstory. The register records the home buyer deck p29 as $2,500,000 in 2013 to $4,200,000. Identical figures and the same city, which is the register own test for re-narration rather than coincidence. Suzy, PROBABLE: investor deck holds 2023, $3,850,000, 2026 value $4,200,000, equity created $350,000, let at $1,800 pw, against the register home buyer figure of a $346,000 client saving. Different measures, four thousand dollars apart, same name and city, and $346,000 appears nowhere in the investor deck.
melbourneThirdProofContested.status: BLOCKING THE THIRD SLOT, NEEDS THE CLIENT
melbourneThirdProofContested.consequence: DESIGN.md puts a contested claim at Tier 3, which does not render, so neither candidate can be published. The page ships with two records and a visibly bracketed third rather than a plausible one. It also widens the deck overlap problem from three records to at least four confirmed, and the two records independently picked as the strongest Melbourne home buyer material are both in it, so the overlap can no longer be read as an isolated oddity.
options: Ask the client to confirm the framing for Stephen and Melanie, which is the strongest Melbourne record in either deck and would be a strong card if the home purchase framing is the true one.
Work through the other 21 Melbourne home buyer records, which needs the home buyer deck back on disk; only the investor deck is there.
Ship with two records, which is the current state, and say so.
melbourneThirdProofContested.alsoDone: The two records that did ship were audited. Geoff does not appear in the investor deck at all. Wendy figures on the page match that deck exactly. Neither carries a contradiction this repository can see.

templateNotFormula.problem: The 21 Aug 2026 work derived this family's structure from the live Brisbane page, because Brisbane performs and was supplied as the reference. That answered "why does Brisbane work" by reading Brisbane alone.
templateNotFormula.decision: Structure is not the ranking variable. /location/melbourne and /location/adelaide were read on 2 Sep 2026 and both run the same HubSpot template as Brisbane: same section order, same award wall, same sitewide testimonial carousel, same six "Why choose us" cards, same FAQ pattern, same office block, same voice. One template, three outcomes, so the section list cannot be what separates them.
templateNotFormula.consequence: The 23 section anatomy in the archived REFERENCE.md is retired as a brief. It is a description of a template three pages share. The thirteen section structure in PLAN.md section 3 replaces it, and it is argued from what each section does for conversion, ranking and answer engines rather than from what Brisbane happens to carry. The Melbourne build of 21 Aug 2026 is archived for the same reason.
templateNotFormula.whatDiffersInstead: PLAN.md section 1.2 tabulates it. Brisbane names more QLD staff, carries a purchases embed, has more regional sub-pages pointing at it and a stronger FAQ than Melbourne. Melbourne is the weakest of the three on local signals despite the largest market, and carries a factual error, "Melbourne's subtropical climate", that an answer engine will quote. Adelaide has the best FAQ of the three and the weakest everything else.
templateNotFormula.openUnderneath: PLAN.md section 1.3 ranks five hypotheses and gives the test for each. H1, competition intensity in Melbourne, is inferred and probably dominant, and if it is, no on-page rebuild closes the Melbourne gap on its own. H2, local authority signals, is the one the rebuild can move. Both need the phase 0 data. Until that data exists the rebuild is proceeding on H2 as an assumption, and the SEO expectation should be set accordingly.

replacementInventory.problem: Melbourne and Adelaide are live, indexed, ranking URLs. Rebuilding a ranking URL is the one way this work goes backwards, because content signals the page currently earns can be dropped without anyone noticing until position moves.
replacementInventory.decision: Before any copy is written for a page that already exists, run the inventory in PLAN.md section 2 against the live page and carry every item into the new page or record why it was dropped. Keep the URL and the self referencing canonical, no redirects. Keep every suburb currently named, adding rather than subtracting. Keep every named local staff member, the office NAP exactly as it appears in GBP, the FAQ questions as query variants, the internal links, and at least ten H2s. Rewrite the strings, keep the terms.
replacementInventory.status: RESOLVED 2 Sep 2026 as the rule. The inventory itself is a phase 2 job
replacementInventory.consequence: tools/extract-live-inventory.mjs is written in phase 2 so this is a diff rather than a reading, and every location COPY.md ends with a preserved-from-live table mapping each inventory item to where it lands or why it went. A page with an unexplained drop does not ship. Perth is exempt: it is a new URL with no inventory to preserve, which is why PLAN.md builds it last.
replacementInventory.deliberateDrops: Recorded in PLAN.md section 2 rather than here, because each needs its replacement named alongside it: the award wall becomes one line with the count and two named wins, the sitewide testimonial carousel becomes Melbourne only testimonials, the purchases iframe becomes three crawlable Tier 1 cards, and the lifestyle, transport and food and wine prose folds its entity names into the market and regions sections.

advocateInRankingLayer.problem: "Buyers' advocate" is the dominant Victorian term and "buyers' agent" is the NSW and QLD term. The design system bans "advocate" in headings and CTAs, and tools/check.mjs enforces that against h1, h2, h3 and button text. The live Melbourne title tag carries both terms; its H1 carries only one. So the rule and the market disagree for Victoria and South Australia specifically.
advocateInRankingLayer.proposal: A two layer split, which the checker already permits without amendment. "Advocate" is allowed in the ranking layer: title tag, meta description, image alt text, schema alternateName and anchor text. It stays out of the persuasion layer: every heading, every button, every CTA. PLAN.md adds one deliberate exception in the persuasion layer, FAQ question 10, "What is the difference between a buyers' agent and a buyers' advocate", which is a real Victorian query and answers itself in a sentence.
advocateInRankingLayer.status: OPEN, RECOMMEND YES. Owner Kenn, with Manu on the volume data. Number 1 in PLAN.md section 8
advocateInRankingLayer.consequence: Blocks the Melbourne and Adelaide title tags, so it blocks phase 2 sign off rather than phase 3. If the answer is no, both pages give up the dominant local term in the field search engines weight most, and the Melbourne title tag loses the thing the live page already gets right.
advocateInRankingLayer.test: Semrush volume for "buyers advocate melbourne" against "buyers agent melbourne". If advocate is twice the volume or more, the ranking layer must carry it.
advocateInRankingLayer.checkerNote: No change to tools/check.mjs is needed to allow this. The existing "advocate" rule reads headings and buttons only, so title and meta are already outside it. Phase 3 tightens the rule the other way, to fail an occurrence anywhere except title, meta, alt text and the FAQ 10 answer.

feePublication.problem: The fee basis is in the client's own onboarding material but is not published on any live location page. Nothing on those pages states a fee, a timeframe or a process, which is why an answer engine can extract an address and a phone number from them and nothing else.
feePublication.proposal: Publish the fee basis plainly in section 8 and in FAQ questions 1 and 2: a fixed fee agreed before the search starts, equivalent to 1.5 to 2 percent of the purchase price for a full search, 1 percent for appraisal and negotiation, and $660 engagement plus a $3,300 success fee for auction bidding only.
feePublication.status: OPEN. Owner Rich via Jason. Number 2 in PLAN.md section 8
feePublication.consequence: This is the strongest single AEO move available on the page, because "how much does a buyers agent cost in Melbourne" is a head question no competitor answers directly, and an answer engine quotes the most specific sourced sentence it can find. It is also a commercial call that this repository does not get to make. Blocks section 8 and FAQ 1 and 2. If the answer is no, those slots ship bracketed rather than vague: a fee section that talks around the number is worse than one that says the number is on request.
feePublication.tier: Tier 1 when published, because it is the client's own pricing schedule. Do not publish a fee figure that is not in that schedule, and do not average or round one.

decksCommitted.decision: The five client success-story decks are committed in paper/decks/ from 8 Sep 2026, at the client lead's direction, so the source of every Tier 1 figure travels with the repository. Until then they were gitignored working files in .deck-src/.
decksCommitted.consequence: tools/extract-deck-images.mjs reads paper/decks/ first and .deck-src/ as a fallback. paper/decks/README.md maps each deck's pages to cities. About 30MB of PDF is now in the repository; the byte-identical '(1)' downloads were not committed. Anyone auditing a register figure can open the page it cites without asking for the file.

adelaideProofFramingContested.problem: Every South Australian record the client has supplied, five in all, appears in both Legacy decks with identical figures: as a home purchase in the homebuyer deck and as an investment in the investor deck. The proof register's 21 Aug rule says a record in more than one deck is Tier 3 until the client says which framing is true.
adelaideProofFramingContested.decision: Render the figures, bracket the framing. The three Adelaide cards carry year, price, 2026 value and equity, which both decks agree on, plus one fact per record that both decks share. The segment pill reads [Home or investment], and nothing on a card says home, investment, yield, rent, saving or time to purchase, since each of those is in only one deck. Karl's quote, identical in both decks and segment neutral, is the one Adelaide testimonial.
adelaideProofFramingContested.status: APPLIED TO THE DESIGN 8 Sep 2026, FRAMING NEEDS THE CLIENT
adelaideProofFramingContested.consequence: This differs from the Melbourne third slot, which stays fully bracketed because that card needed to be a home buyer record. Adelaide's cards make no segment claim, so the uncontested figures can stand. One answer per record from Rich (home or investment for Karl, Peter and Li) clears all three pills. The July 2026 decks show the same re-narration across seven Sydney records, so the question is now about how the client writes decks, not about individual records.

julyDecksCarryNoSaOrWa.finding: The three decks supplied 8 Sep 2026 (July 2026 Homebuyers, July 2026 Investors, Latest Commercial) cover Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Gold Coast, regional NSW, VIC and QLD, and one Hobart record. No Adelaide, no Perth. The Adelaide proof therefore comes from the two Legacy decks, and Perth stays at zero.
julyDecksCarryNoSaOrWa.consequence: The July decks are still useful: they carry month and year on every record, which the Legacy decks do not, and 25 new Melbourne home buyer records that the Melbourne third proof slot could be filled from once the cross deck check is run against the July investor deck. That is a Melbourne job, not started here.

perthVariantInPaper.decision: The Perth artboard was updated to the PLAN.md section 5 variant on 8 Sep 2026 even though phase 6 is blocked: proof section rewritten as 'How we buy in Perth' with three cards of cleared Tier 2 facts and one bracketed named-agent slot, the local team section deleted, the office block deleted, two region cards and four testimonial cards deleted, and 'Do you have an office in Perth?' answered honestly in the FAQ.
perthVariantInPaper.status: RESOLVED 8 Sep 2026 for the design; the HTML build stays blocked per locations/perth/BLOCKED.md
perthVariantInPaper.consequence: The client reviews the honest page and sees the three gaps as brackets, which is a better prompt for supplying a name and a purchase than a note. The card photographs are Perth streetscapes and are named '(not a purchase)' in the layer tree so nobody mistakes them for proof. Everything deleted is recoverable from Paper's version history and the Melbourne artboard.

adelaideAgentCards.problem: PLAN.md 4.2 and section 5 say do not pad the local team with the executive or national team, and that a single SA agent makes the section 'Your Adelaide buyers' agent'. The client-approved Melbourne artboard shows seven cards, five of them Sydney and Brisbane people.
adelaideAgentCards.decision: Follow the approved artboard. Jonathon Moore replaces Amanda Jones and moves to card 1; the other six carry over. COPY.md flags the single-agent alternative for the client.
adelaideAgentCards.consequence: Matching the approved template is the reversible choice; the client has already accepted national cards on Melbourne. If they prefer the honest single card, deleting six cards is a smaller change than rebuilding a section.

languagePass8Sep.decision: Both new artboards were read end to end for Australian English, punctuation and terminal full stops on 8 Sep 2026, and the rules are written down in locations/adelaide/COPY.md under 'Language pass'. Full stops on every sentence of body copy including inside brackets, none on fragments (suburb lists, stat labels, field labels, captions, fee values, the reviewed byline). 'A buyer's agent' singular, 'buyers' agents' plural. 'Off-market' hyphenated before a noun, open elsewhere.
languagePass8Sep.status: APPLIED TO ADELAIDE AND PERTH 8 Sep 2026
languagePass8Sep.found: One material error: the Perth section heading still read 'Perth purchases' above three cards that state there are no Perth purchases, because the earlier rewrite to 'How we buy in Perth' had not taken. Set again and verified by screenshot. Also corrected across the two pages: eleven plural-possessive errors, four hyphenation errors, a comma splice in the Adelaide proof intro, 'the Barossa' against its own 'Barossa Valley' card, 'the Hills' in an Adelaide FAQ, 'mixed use' as a bare noun, a tense mix in a Perth card, 'yet' in the Perth intro implying an office is coming, a Perth testimonials H2 that was not in query form, an Australian city listed among expat bases, and '[nearest office] office' saying office twice in five places.
languagePass8Sep.consequence: A Paper set_text_content call can echo the value it was given without the node taking it. Verify a heading rewrite by reading it back, not by the tool response. This is the second design-side check that has to be a read-back rather than a trust.
